data.body:
SUPERSEDED by S4 (reluctant-undeniable-crane / f371-ca39-181c-4091).

The Gerrit code review of S4's change 1947 returned LLM-Review -1 with a correct blocking
finding: `src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md` quotes coach move 14's template
VERBATIM and is served verbatim to users by `rebar explain plan` / MCP. S4 cut that template
over to [non-codebase], so splitting the guide into this separate story left the SHIPPED guide
misquoting its own coach output at S4's commit — a regression judged on that change's own
merits, not excused by the stack landing together later.

The plan-review gate had flagged the same coupling earlier and I mistakenly argued the
inconsistency was contained within the stack. It was not.

All of this story's scope is therefore folded into S4 and has landed there:
- the guide cut over to [non-codebase] (0 remaining legacy mentions; its verbatim quote of the
  move-14 template now matches the live template exactly),
- `tests/unit/test_guides.py::test_operator_attested_tag_documented` renamed and flipped to
  `test_non_codebase_tag_documented` asserting [non-codebase],
- NEW `test_legacy_alias_stays_undocumented`, which is what makes ADR 0101's 'accepted but
  UNDOCUMENTED alias' actually enforceable rather than aspirational — without it the legacy
  spelling drifts back into the author guide and the rename quietly un-does itself.

No scope is dropped.
